paragraphs.text: Lesson 10. At the amusement park.
Jennifer and Ben are at an amusement park, but they have very different ideas about how to have fun there.
Listen to their conversation and mark the statements true or false.
Come on Jennifer, let's go and ride the screamer. It'll be a blast.
Count me out. I'm not going on a ride where I have to sign a waiver stating that if I die the amusement park isn't responsible.
But the screamer is the park's main attraction. It'll get your heart pumping. That's for sure.
How about the bumper cars, huh? Bumper cars are fun. And then maybe we can ride the ferris wheel. That's about as much adrenaline as I can handle.
It's not like you'll be perfectly safe on the bumper cars. You could get whiplash, you know.
Okay, smart guy, then how about doing something simple? Let's go get a hot dog. I'm starving.
Me too, but I'd rather ride the screamer on an empty stomach. Maybe afterwards we can grab a snack.
That's exactly what I'm talking about. Why on earth would you want to go on a ride that's pretty much guaranteed to make you puke?
I'm going to go watch the clowns and munch on a corn dog.
Are you really going to pass up the chance to go on the screamer? It's the world's fastest ride where you're upside down the whole time.
People flock to this park for miles away just to ride it.
Ben, I like to enjoy myself with the amusement park. Meaning I will not get on a roller coaster that's basically a brush with death.
But if that's your idea of fun, then go ahead. Be my guest.
Come on, you gotta get out of your comfort zone. Live it up a little.
This year it's the screamer and next year it will be something else. What was it last time? Oh yeah, the ozone drop.
And if I recall correctly, after you got off that ride, you nearly passed out.
Yeah, but man, what a ride. I got dropped 10 stories at 150 miles an hour. Good times.
Whatever floats your boat. Go on. Go ride the screamer and meet me back here in an hour. I'll be here with my feet firmly planted on the ground.
You'll be here with a red balloon giggling about the dorky clowns.
Oh well, your loss. I'm going to get in line for the screamer.
And I'm going to enjoy my clowns and hot dogs. Don't you just love the amusement park? It has something for everyone.
True. Okay. See you in an hour.
Let's learn the vocabulary from today's dialogue.
Ben says, come on, Jennifer. Let's go and ride the screamer. It will be a blast.
A blast is a slang way to say a great time. Lots of fun.
But Jennifer says, count me out.
This expression, count me out, means I'm not going to participate.
Jennifer says, I'm not going on a ride where I have to sign a waiver.
A waiver is a document where you agree to give up some rights.
In this case, the document states that if Jennifer dies on the ride, the amusement park isn't responsible.
Ben says that the screamer will get your heart pumping.
Pumping, in this case, means beating very fast.
But Jennifer suggests two calmer rides, the bumper cars and the ferris wheel.
She says, that's about as much adrenaline as I can handle.
Adrenaline means excitement, especially from danger.
Ben points out that the bumper cars aren't perfectly safe. He says, you could get whiplash, you know.
Whiplash is an injury to your neck caused by a sudden start or stop motion.
Whiplash is a common injury in car accidents when there's a sudden impact.
So Jennifer suggests going and getting a hot dog. She says, I'm starving.
This is an exaggerated way to say, I'm extremely hungry.
But Ben says he would prefer to ride the screamer on an empty stomach.
Maybe afterwards we can grab a snack.
The verb grab is an informal word for get. Grab can also mean to take something with your hand.
Jennifer asks, why on earth would you want to go on a ride that's pretty much guaranteed to make you puke?
The word puke is a slang way to say vomit.
Jennifer says, I'm going to go watch the clowns and munch on a corn dog.
The word munch on means to eat casually.
Ben asks her, are you really going to pass up the chance to go on the screamer?
Pass up the chance means not take advantage of the opportunity.
Why is the screamer so special?
Ben says, it's the world's fastest ride where you're upside down the whole time.
Upside down means inverted.
Your feet are in the air and your head is pointed down towards the ground.
Ben says, people flock to this park for miles away just to ride it.
The word flock means to come and gather in large numbers.
But Jennifer says that this roller coaster is basically a brush with death.
A brush with death means an instance of nearly dying.
But she says, if that's your idea of fun then go ahead, be my guest.
Be my guest means do what you want.
Ben tries to convince Jennifer by saying, come on, you gotta get out of your comfort zone.
Getting out of your comfort zone means to try different things that may make you a little bit uncomfortable.
Ben also says, live it up a little.
Live it up means to enjoy yourself often extravagantly.
Another example of living it up would be going out and partying a lot and spending a lot of money on parties and expensive alcohol.
It's enjoying yourself in an extravagant way.
Jennifer remembers that last year, after Ben rode the ozone drop, he nearly passed out.
The phrasal verb passed out means fainted, lost consciousness.
But Ben loved the ride.
He says, I got dropped 10 stories at 150 miles an hour.
The word stories refers to floors or levels of a building.
Jennifer responds, whatever floats your boat, this means whatever makes you happy.
We usually use this expression when we think that the thing that makes the other person happy is a little bit strange or unusual.
Jennifer refuses to ride the screamer, and Ben says, you'll be here with the red balloon giggling about the dorky clowns.
The word giggling means laughing with short, high-pitched sounds.
Giggling is often associated with female laughter.
The word dorky means stupid or silly.
Then he says, oh well, your loss.
Your loss means you are the one who is missing a good opportunity.
What do you think? Are you more like Ben, or are you more like Jennifer?
That's all the vocabulary from today's conversation.
